summary: steam demos rows carry parent_tags (the full game's tag names) because demos almost never have tags of their own; the parent lookup returns name AND tags in the one GetItems request the page already made, so the budget stays at 3 requests per page.
reason: Live measurement: 0 of 100 demos carried store tags, while 100 of 100 of their full games did, so a demos row showed an empty tag column exactly when the caller needed the game's genre signal. Folding tags into the existing parent GetItems request (include_tag_count: 20, Steam's per-item cap) keeps the request budget unchanged. A regen that reverts to AppNames or drops include_tag_count reintroduces empty tag columns or a 4th request; the compact keep-set must also retain parent_tags, which is sparse whenever parents do not resolve.
validated_outcome: Offline tests pass: parent_tags equals the full game's tag names in order; a 5-demo/3-parent page issues exactly 3 requests and the GetItems data_request carries include_tag_count; parent_appid 0 and hidden parents yield rows with null parent_tags and no parent_name while resolvable rows stay populated; --agent compaction keeps parent_tags; temporarily dropping include_tag_count makes TestDemosParentTagsFromFullGame fail.
